title: Story
intro: From church in Brooklyn to the Oscars, year by year.
seo_description: Miles Caton's story year by year, from gospel roots and a viral 'Feeling Good' to Sinners, the Oscars and Columbia Records.

opener.headline: Raised in
opener.text: His mother and his aunt are gospel singers. He started singing in church at two.

entries.title: Sam Cooke at the gala
entries.body: On stage at an NAACP Freedom Fund awards gala in New York, singing a Sam Cooke song at five years old.

entries.title: “Feeling Good” goes viral
entries.body: His cover of the Nina Simone standard gets sampled in the opening montage of Jay-Z's “4:44” video.

entries.title: *Little Big Shots,* twice
entries.body: “For Every Mountain” on the season three premiere, then “O Holy Night” for the NBC holiday special.

entries.title: Live on *The View*
entries.body: “Never Give Up” on Martin Luther King Jr. Day, sung alongside Yolanda Adams.

entries.title: On the road with H.E.R.
entries.body: A tour first, then he came home and finished high school.

entries.title: “This Ain't It”
entries.body: His debut single. He directed the music video himself.

entries.title: *Sinners*
entries.body: His first feature. He plays Sammie Moore opposite Michael B. Jordan, and gets a Critics' Choice win for it.
entries.caption: World premiere, with Michael B. Jordan
entries.alt: Miles Caton with Michael B. Jordan at the Sinners world premiere

entries.title: The Oscars, then Columbia
entries.body: A BAFTA Rising Star nomination, then “I Lied to You” live at the Oscars. In March he signs with Columbia and puts out “Don't Hate Me”; “Lean On” follows in August.
entries.caption: Critics' Choice, Best Young Performer
entries.alt: Miles Caton accepting the Critics' Choice award for Best Young Performer
